 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, it is taken up for final disposal, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties.

2. This appeal is by the North-West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (NWKRTC) disputing the quantum of compensation awarded and the negligence under the judgment and award dated 08.12.2021 passed in MVC No.91/2020 by the learned IV Addl.Senior Civil Judge and Addl.MACT,
Dharwad (for short, 'Tribunal').
3.

The claimants being the parents of deceased Kasim @ Kashimsab, preferred a claim petition under Section 166(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the accidental death of Kasim @ Kashimsab that took place on 09.02.2020 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25/Y-6399 and bus bearing registration No.KA-29/F-2927.
It is pleaded that the deceased was aged 27 years as on the date of the accident and he was a mechanic, earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
On issuance of notice, respondent appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the petition averments.
It is contended that the accident was due to negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
It is further contended that the rider of the motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the motorcycle.
As the accident occurred due to negligence of the rider of the motorcycle, the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.
5. Before the Tribunal, 1st claimant-mother of the deceased examined herself as PW1 and marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P10.
On behalf of respondent, driver of the bus was examined as RW1 and marked documents as Exs.R1 to R12.

sentences.text: The Tribunal on examination of the material on record arrived at a conclusion that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus.
The Tribunal awarded a total compensation at Rs.23,14,800/- with interest at 8% per annum under following heads.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:3821-DB Sl.No. Heads Calculation 1 Towards loss of dependency Rs.22,84,800/-
2 Towards loss of estate and Rs.30,000/-
 funeral expenses 3

Total compensation awarded Rs.23,14,800/-
7.

The Tribunal while determining the compensation assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.12,000/- per month, deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses, added 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

8. Heard Sri. M.C.Hukkeri, learned counsel for the appellant-insurer as well as Sri. T.M.Nadaf,
learned counsel for claimants-respondents.
9. Learned counsel for the insurer submits that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle.
Hence, the appellant is not liable to pay any compensation.

It is further submitted that by referring to the Ex.P3-spot mahazar contends that it is the two wheeler which has entered in a negligent manner to the main road, due to which the accident has occurred.
The driver of the bus has taken utmost care while driving the bus.
Hence no negligence on the part of driver of the bus.
The Tribunal NC: 2024:KHC-D:3821-DB committed an error in holding that accident caused due to negligence of the driver of the bus.
Thus prays to set aside the award.
10. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants submits that the charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the bus.
The digital evidence relied on by the Corporation cannot be referred to, as no certificate required under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act is produced.
Further learned counsel submits that even if the negligence is on the rider of the motorcycle, the deceased being pillion rider, the claimants are entitled for compensation for death of the deceased.
It is further submitted that the notional income assessed by the Tribunal is on lower side, the same is to be considered at Rs.13,750/- per month.

11. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers, the points that arise for consideration are as under:
i.
Whether the Tribunal is justified in holding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driver of the bus?

3 NC: 2024:KHC-D:3821-DB ii.

entities.text: Divisional Controller vs Maiharunissa W/O Mahammed Ajim Shaikh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal needs reconsideration?
12. Our answer to the above points are 'in the affirmative' for the following reasons.
13. The death of Sri Kasim @ Kashimsab on 09.02.2020 involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-25/Y-6399 and bus bearing No.KA-29/F-2927 is not in dispute in this appeal.
14. The contention of the appellant that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle cannot be accepted.
As per Ex.P3-spot sketch, it is clear that the two wheeler has entered the main road from petrol bunk on the other side of the road.
The bus before reaching the accident place has to cross a curve road.

By considering the width, may be of the road being curvy,
distance at which the accident has taken place, it cannot be accepted that the driver of the bus has taken reasonable care while passing the curve on the main road.

Further, the Tribunal on examination of the evidence placed by the respondent at Ex.R12 has recorded a finding that the image of the motorcycle and bus NC: 2024:KHC-D:3821-DB appeared in the said video is not identifiable.
It is further recorded that the motorcycle joined the road and proceed further and then bus has came from behind.
The above finding on the basis of the evidence placed by the Corporation itself, is clear that before the bus reaching the accident place, the two wheeler has already entered the main road.
The Corporation except relying on Ex.P3/spot sketch, no other evidence is placed to prove that the accident in question was due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle.
As per Ex.P5-Motor Vehicles Accident Report damage is caused to the front side of the bus and on rear side to the motorcycle.
This would prove that bus has dashed motorcycle.
In such circumstances, we are of the view that the Tribunal is justified in holding that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus.
15. In the absence of any proof to prove the income of the deceased, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.12,000/- per month
as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services NC: 2024:KHC-D:3821-DB Authority, for the accident of the year 2020 the notional income is to be assessed at Rs.13,750/- per month.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services NC: 2024:KHC-D:3821-DB Authority
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, we assess the income of the deceased at Rs.13,750/- per month.
It is not in dispute that the deceased was a bachelor.
The Tribunal committed an error in deducting 1/3rd of the assessed income towards personal expenses.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another1 when the deceased was bachelor 50% of the assessed income is to be deducted towards personal expenses.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others2, the Tribunal rightly increased assessed income by 40% towards future prospects.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Both the claimants being parents are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards consortium.
The claimants are entitled Rs.15,000/- under the head loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- under the head funeral expenses.
As per Pranay Sethi, consortium, loss of estate and funeral (2009) 6 SCC 121 (2017) 6 SCC 680 NC: 2024:KHC-D:3821-DB expenses are to be increased by 10%.

Thus the claimants would be entitled for compensation on the head of loss of dependency at Rs.19,63,500/-
(Rs.13,750 + 40% less 50% x 12 x 17).

The Tribunal committed an error in awarding interest @ 8% per annum.
Considering the prevailing Bank interest, we deem it appropriate to award interest at 6% per annum.

Thus, the total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as under:

2 Loss
of parental consortium Rs.88,000/-

3 Loss of estate and funeral Rs.33,000/-
 expenses  Total Rs.20,84,500/-
17. Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.20,84,500/- as against Rs.23,14,800/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The above appeal is disposed off.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3821-DB b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation Rs.20,84,500/- as against Rs.23,14,800/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The compensation amount will bear interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.
d) The respondent/Corporation shall pay the entire compensation amount along with accrued interest in favour of the claimants.
e) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement of the enhanced compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
f) Draw modified award accordingly.
g) Registry to transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.

- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:3821-DB h) The amount in deposit, if any is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal.
